item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 020531
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Tue Sep 1 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula, on Hurricane Lowell, located several hundred
miles south-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands, and on Tropical
Storm Marie, located several hundred miles south of the southern
tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form well offshore of southwestern
Mexico over the weekend. Gradual development is possible early
next week as the system moves west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph,
and is likely to remain well offshore of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

&&

header WTPZ33 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Marie are issued under WMO
header WTPZ23 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP3.

$$

THE PACIFIC...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.5N 131.7W
ABOUT 1440 MI...2315 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...145 MPH...230 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...940 MB...27.76 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was
located near latitude 18.5 North, longitude 131.7 West. Karina is
moving toward the west near 12 mph (19 km/h), and a westward to 
west-northwestward motion is expected over the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 145 mph (230 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Karina is a category 4 hurricane on the 
Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale.  Some additional strengthening 
is possible through Wednesday morning, followed by slow weakening 
over the next several days.  However, Karina is likely to remain a 
major hurricane into Thursday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 940 mb (27.76 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 24
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Tue Sep 01 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 020843
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  24
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
1100 PM HST Tue Sep 01 2026
 
Karina's satellite presentation is even a little more impressive 
than it was earlier today.  The hurricane is exhibiting a 
well-defined 25 n mi diameter eye embedded in very deep convection.  
The eye temperature on satellite imagery has warmed to around 16 deg 
C over the past several hours. Using a blend of objective satellite 
estimates, the advisory intensity is set at 125 kt.  This is close 
to the latest DPRINT value from UW-CIMSS.  Karina's cloud pattern is 
quite symmetrical and is typical of an annular hurricane.

Karina continues moving just slightly north of due west, or around 
280/10 kt.  The track forecast philosophy is basically unchanged 
from the previous few advisories.  The flow on the southern side of 
a narrow mid-tropospheric ridge should continue to steer the system 
on a westward to west-northwestward course for the next 3 days or 
so.  Later in the forecast period, a more northwestward track is 
likely due to the influence of a mid-level cyclone to the north of 
Hawaii.  The new official forecast is very similar to the previous 
NHC track and is a blend of the latest ECMWF, HCCA, and Google 
DeepMind predictions.  There is fairly high confidence that Karina 
will pass to the north of the Hawaiian Islands.

Karina remains over marginally warm waters with low vertical wind 
shear.  Therefore, the hurricane has an opportunity for some 
additional strengthening during the next 12 hours or so.  A gradual 
weakening trend should commence thereafter due to drier air and 
somewhat cooler waters.  However, since Karina appears to be 
an annular hurricane, its weakening during the forecast period is 
likely to be slower than normal.  The official intensity forecast 
is generally above the model guidance owing to the annular nature 
of the system.  Karina is likely to maintain hurricane strength for 
at least the next 72 hours.

...MARIE FORECAST TO BECOME A HURRICANE LATER TODAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM MST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.7N 111.0W
ABOUT 435 MI...700 KM S OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 310 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Marie was
located near latitude 16.7 North, longitude 111.0 West. Marie is
moving toward the northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h). A turn toward the
west-northwest is expected later today, and that motion should
continue through Friday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Some strengthening is forecast during the next 48 hours, 
and Marie is likely to become a hurricane later today.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 185 miles (295 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will affect portions of the coast
of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next
few days and will likely spread northward to southern California
over the weekend.  These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office. A depiction of rip current
risk for the United States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Tropical Storm Marie Forecast Discussion Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Wed Sep 02 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 020844
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Marie Discussion Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 AM MST Wed Sep 02 2026

Satellite imagery shows that Marie continues to produce deep 
convection near the center, with a large curved band in the 
southeastern semicircle of the storm.  An earlier microwave image 
did show that the inner core remains in the primitive stages of 
development, though that was several hours ago now.  Intensity 
estimates are about the same as the last cycle, so the current winds 
will remain 55 kt.  

Marie remains on a northwestward heading tonight, steered by a 
distant ridge over Mexico.  The ridge is forecast to build westward 
later this week, which will likely force Marie to move more towards 
the west-northwest.  Track uncertainty is high by the weekend due 
to an approaching mid-latitude trough over the eastern Pacific, 
though the bulk of the guidance show this trough missing the storm. 
The new NHC forecast is very similar to the previous one, showing 
the west-northwestward track at the end of the forecast, and lying 
near the typically reliable HCCA and GDMI consensus aids.

The storm has a couple of days over very warm waters within light 
shear for intensification.  The biggest current hindrance is 
probably the earlier-observed broad microwave structure, though 
very deep convection is near the center.  Thus the NHC forecast 
will stay on the aggressive side of the guidance, and little 
change is made to the previous forecast.  By the weekend, Marie is 
forecast to move over cooler SSTs and into a drier, more stable air 
mass, which should induce a gradual weakening trend.
